Date: 2026-11-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Cerulean Head of Security), Ethan Cole (Cerulean CTO), Rochi Patel (Cerulean Compliance), Samir Gupta (Cerulean Platform) 
Recording: Yes
summary: Cerulean requested a posture readout covering Redwood's SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts, Trust Center access model, RBAC/SSO mapping options, audit log retention/export patterns, and KMS integration (customer-managed keys/HSM). Meeting covered available artifacts, evidence handoff options, and an initial plan for a controlled pilot (VPC + dedicated) and proof of evidence export. Several clarifications on redaction, residency (EU/US regions), and long-term log retention were captured.
topics: SOC 2 Type II report availability and redaction
Trust Center vs manual evidence delivery
RBAC model and SCIM/SAML for SSO
Audit log retention/export and SIEM integration
KMS / customer-managed keys and HSM requirements
Pilot: dedicated VPC vs Hosted with private endpoints
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. um we know the ask is a posture readout and then to plan how you want the evidence handed off.
[00:08] Maya Ortiz: hi alex, thanks. we're mainly trying to understand what we can include in our vendor pack for ISO and also make sure SOC 2 aligns with our internal roster, so two things: 1) evidence access and 2) key management.
[00:20] Priya Desai: great. quick intro from our side, i'm priya, solutions engineer. i'll walk through the technical controls and how they map to the trust center and options for manual export.
[00:30] Ethan Cole: hi, ethan here. i mostly care about residency and the KMS/HSM flow—can you support a customer-managed key in a hardware module?
[00:38] Priya Desai: yes, we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed via bring-your-own-key in a few patterns. the standard is cloud KMS with envelope encryption; for HSM the flow is... uh, we usually integrate via a key wrapping approach and you hold the root. there is a slight config difference if you want on-prem hsm vs cloud hsm.
[00:56] Samir Gupta: are there latency implications if keys are in another region? we need sub-200 ms token decryption for inference in the eu-west region.
[01:04] Priya Desai: there can be a latency hit, correct, especially if the HSM calls are synchronous per request. we recommend a short-lived session token or a local key cache. note: our KV cache was referenced as KV cash earlier in some notes, that is the same thing—it's used to reduce repeated KMS round trips.
[01:20] Maya Ortiz: okay that's helpful. on SOC2, do you have a Type II report that we can give to auditors? and is there a shared trust portal?
[01:28] Alex Chen: yes we've got a SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert. we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II and an ISO summary. we also have a Trust Center — sometimes shown as Trustcenter on older PDFs — that hosts control mappings, evidence indexes, and some downloadable artifacts.
[01:44] Maya Ortiz: are the control mappings exportable? we want to map Redwood controls to our control matrix for clause alignment.
[01:50] Priya Desai: absolutely. we can export a CSV that maps our control ids to common frameworks. we will also provide a mapping doc for ISO 27001 annex A items.
[02:00] Ethan Cole: about log retention — what's the default retention for audit logs and can we push them to our SIEM?
[02:06] Priya Desai: by default platform audit logs are retained 90 days. for enterprise customers we have configurable retention and a push/export API to stream logs to your SIEM or S3. we also support periodic snapshots via secure sftp. note that the audit log schema is in the trust center docs.
[02:24] Maya Ortiz: perfect. for long term retention we might need seven years for some regulated datasets; can you export in a compressed signed format?
[02:31] Priya Desai: yes we can provide signed log archives (gz) and deliver via SFTP or our secure artifact portal. we'll need to discuss retention costs — long-term storage is billed separately.
[02:40] Samir Gupta: on SSO, what does the RBAC look like? we run okta and want SCIM provisioning if possible.
[02:46] Alex Chen: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. roles in the console map to RBAC groups; you can set minimal privileges by route/model, and there are token-level controls.
[02:56] Priya Desai: important nuance: API keys can be scoped to routes and models, but if you use SCIM provisioning the user groups sync to those console roles. sometimes the naming in the trust center is inconsistent — you'll see group names and role ids both.
[03:12] Ethan Cole: is there MFA enforced on the admin accounts? auditors will want multifactor.
[03:16] Alex Chen: yes, MFA is enforced for admin-level users; SSO enforces your provider policy as well. we also have org-wide session timeout and conditional access.
[03:26] Maya Ortiz: on evidence delivery - we prefer to avoid giving auditor accounts direct trustcenter access. can you do a manual evidence handoff?
[03:34] Priya Desai: yes we commonly do manual handoffs. options: 1) limited Trust Center access with read-only, IP-restrict and time-boxed links; 2) provide a redacted report and per-request artifact bundles delivered over SFTP; or 3) a shared artifact drop with signed URLs.
[03:54] Maya Ortiz: sounds good. which of those is most common for healthcare customers?
[03:58] Alex Chen: healthcare customers often choose SFTP handoff plus minimal trustcenter access for controls that change frequently. also we do an evidence handoff call where the SE walks auditors through the artifacts.
[04:10] Samir Gupta: any automated evidence collection—like a report that shows control evidence for a date range?
[04:15] Priya Desai: we have an evidence export tool that can produce timelines and snapshots. it's part of Redwood Console's compliance toolkit — sometimes called Redwood Optimum in notes — it creates a package of logs, config snapshots, and change history. the export can be filtered by time range and redaction rules.
[04:31] Ethan Cole: KMS question again — if we bring our keys, does Redwood ever see plaintext?
[04:36] Priya Desai: no. with BYOK the root never leaves your HSM. Redwood stores wrapped keys and performs decryption operations when authorized. there is a short-lived unwrapped cache at the runtime layer for performance, but we can configure it to be in-memory only and ephemeral. auditors like to see that mem-only cache config documented.
[04:56] Maya Ortiz: can you capture that cache behavior in a control narrative? we'll need it for ISO.
[05:00] Priya Desai: yes we can include a control narrative and a flow diagram.
[05:04] Alex Chen: quick note on residency — you mentioned EU and US; we can pin workloads to a region (eu-west, us-east) and ensure logs and keys stay in-region depending on the deployment model. for dedicated VPC we can guarantee region isolation.
[05:18] Samir Gupta: if we do private deployment, is there a difference in how evidence is delivered?
[05:22] Priya Desai: private deployments often involve more manual artifact collection because some telemetry is on-prem. we provide a collector and playbook for generating artifacts. we also do assisted evidence extraction in those cases.
[05:34] Maya Ortiz: okay last bit: do you have references or a recent healthcare SOC 2 customer we can call?
[05:40] Alex Chen: yes we can share references — i'll include a short list in the follow up, with permission.
[05:44] Ethan Cole: great. next steps?
[05:46] Alex Chen: recap: we will share the redacted SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary, Priya will send the control mapping CSV and evidence export instructions, Samir will confirm KMS/HSM requirements and preferred delivery path, and we'll schedule a hands-on evidence handoff session next week.
[05:58] Maya Ortiz: that works. thanks everyone.
[06:00] Alex Chen: thanks all. we'll send the deck and the trustcenter link after this call.
[06:04] (end)
